newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia union bans are across the board.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia union bans are across the board.

text.p: Maritime Union of Australia bans on Indonesian cargo and shipping will first hit an Australian wheat cargo but will apply across the board to all commodities, Vic Slater, assistant national secretary of the union, told Reuters.
"It delays things. In terms of the economy, I don't think it has any effect on the Australian economy," he said. "It just buggers up shipping lines."
Slater said an analysis had not been conducted of what other ships and commodities would be hit by the bans.
"We will be looking closely at it," he said.
"It will apply to any Indonesian ship and selected Indonesian cargos," he said.
The first ship to be hit would be the Bogasari Empat, due to arrive in Fremantle, Western Australia, on Wednesday to load 32,500 tonnes of wheat.
The union ban would not stop ships from being loaded but would delay their leaving port for up to 24 hours.
The Bogasari Empat is scheduled to be loaded on Thursday.
"If they hit us it will be tomorrow (Thursday)," Kevin Clark, an official of Monson Shipping Agency, agent for the Bogasari Empat, told Reuters.
The Indonesian ship has been contracted by the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) and regularly plies the Indonesia-Australia run.
The AWB had no immediate comment on the union bans, applied to protest the arrest of two Indonesian independent labour leaders.
